rationale: Matthew 9:27-33 names no prophet and uses no citation formula. What it shares with Isaiah 35:5-6 is a pairing in sequence: blind men whose "eyes were opened" (9:30, BSB) are followed at once by a mute man who "began to speak" (9:33, BSB), where Isaiah says "the eyes of the blind will be opened" and "the mute tongue will shout for joy" (35:5-6, BSB). The tie is made more openly two chapters later, when Jesus answers John's question with "The blind receive sight" (11:5, BSB) -- words Meyer (via the Biblehub aggregator) calls "an echo of Isaiah 35:5 f." Novakovic's publisher description says Matthew makes the healing "Son of David" intelligible through "selected biblical passages, especially from the Book of Isaiah," but that description does not name Isaiah 35. Graded plausible, not strong, because the clearest pointer is a later verse (11:5) and "eyes opened" is common language, not wording unique to Isaiah 35.
